project.name: CICaDo
project.description: CICaDo is an open-source, self-hostable CI/CD platform built around three differentiators: operational simplicity, ChatOps-native control, and AI-agent-native tooling. Two Go binaries — a server with an embedded HTTP UI and a remote runner agent — back a design where PostgreSQL is the only stateful dependency and also acts as the job queue (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + LISTEN/NOTIFY),

nodes.name: postgres.go
nodes.summary: Postgres-backed secrets.Store: encrypts secret values with AES-256-GCM before persisting them in the `secrets` table, scoped to org or (org,repo), resolving repo-scoped secrets before falling back to org-scoped, via a SELECT-FOR-UPDATE-then-insert/update transaction (expression indices block ON CONFLICT).

nodes.name: NewPostgres
nodes.summary: Constructs a Postgres secrets store with the given store handle and encryption key; the lease expiry defaults to 5 minutes.

nodes.name: Put
nodes.summary: Stores or overwrites an encrypted secret for (org, [repo], name) inside a SELECT-FOR-UPDATE-then-insert/update transaction, since the table's expression unique index does not support ON CONFLICT.

nodes.name: Get
nodes.summary: Returns a decrypted Lease for a secret name, trying the repo-scoped row first (if a repo is given) and falling back to the org-scoped row.

nodes.name: makeLease
nodes.summary: Decrypts a ciphertext blob and wraps it in a Lease with a fresh expiry.

nodes.name: Delete
nodes.summary: Deletes a secret row scoped to repo (if repoID given) or org.

nodes.name: List
nodes.summary: Returns the de-duplicated union of org-scoped and (if a repo is given) repo-scoped secret names, values never included.

nodes.name: seal
nodes.summary: AES-256-GCM encrypts plaintext into a nonce||ciphertext||tag blob with a freshly generated random nonce.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: AES-256-GCM decrypts a nonce||ciphertext||tag blob back to plaintext.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Excludes git metadata, docs, generated binaries, and infrastructure directories from the Docker build context so image builds stay small and fast.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Docker build that compiles all three CICaDo binaries once, then produces two purpose-built runtime images: a minimal distroless server image with no shell, and a debian-slim runner image carrying git and a shell for executing job steps.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build shares one golang:1.26 build stage across two distinct minimal runtime targets selected via `--target server` / `--target runner`; the runner intentionally carries more (git, shell, non-root user) than the distroless server because the shell executor needs it.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: golang:1.26 build stage that compiles cicado-server, cicado-runner, and the cicado CLI as static CGO-disabled Linux binaries.

nodes.name: server
nodes.summary: Final distroless/static runtime image for cicado-server; no shell, minimal attack surface, exposes 8080 and 9090.

nodes.name: runner
nodes.summary: Final debian:12-slim runtime image for cicado-runner, with git and ca-certificates installed and a non-root UID 65532 user, since the shell executor and CloneCredentialsForRun need a real shell and git.

nodes.name: FROM golang:1.26 AS build
nodes.summary: Starts the build stage from the golang:1.26 image, required because go.mod's go directive needs >= 1.26 with GOTOOLCHAIN=local.

nodes.name: WORKDIR /src
nodes.summary: Sets the build-stage working directory to /src.

nodes.name: COPY go.mod go.sum ./
nodes.summary: Copies only the module files first so `go mod download` can be cached independently of source changes.

nodes.name: RUN go mod download
nodes.summary: Downloads Go module dependencies into the build-stage module cache.

nodes.name: COPY . .
nodes.summary: Copies the full build context (filtered by .dockerignore) into the build stage.

nodes.name: RUN go build -o /bin/cicado-server
nodes.summary: Builds the statically linked, CGO-disabled cicado-server binary from ./server/cmd/cicado-server.

nodes.name: RUN go build -o /bin/cicado-runner
nodes.summary: Builds the statically linked, CGO-disabled cicado-runner binary from ./runner/cmd/cicado-runner.

nodes.name: RUN go build -o /bin/cicado
nodes.summary: Builds the statically linked, CGO-disabled cicado CLI binary from ./cmd/cicado.

nodes.name: FROM gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot AS server
nodes.summary: Starts the server runtime stage from a minimal, shell-less distroless base image.

nodes.name: COPY --from=build /bin/cicado-server /cicado-server
nodes.summary: Copies the compiled cicado-server binary from the build stage into the server runtime image.

nodes.name: EXPOSE 8080 9090
nodes.summary: Documents the server image's HTTP (8080) and gRPC (9090) listener ports.

nodes.name: ENTRYPOINT ["/cicado-server"]
nodes.summary: Sets the server image's entrypoint to the cicado-server binary.

nodes.name: FROM debian:12-slim AS runner
nodes.summary: Starts the runner runtime stage from debian:12-slim, the smallest Debian base that ships git and a shell.

nodes.name: RUN apt-get update && \
nodes.summary: Installs git and ca-certificates into the runner image and clears the apt cache to keep the layer small.

nodes.name: RUN useradd --uid 65532 --shell /bin/bash --create-home cicado
nodes.summary: Creates the non-root `cicado` user (UID 65532) the runner process runs as.

nodes.name: USER cicado
nodes.summary: Switches the runner image to the non-root cicado user for all subsequent instructions and at runtime.

nodes.name: WORKDIR /home/cicado
nodes.summary: Sets the runner image's working directory to the cicado user's home directory.

nodes.name: COPY --from=build /bin/cicado-runner /home/cicado/cicado-runner
nodes.summary: Copies the compiled cicado-runner binary from the build stage into the runner runtime image.

nodes.name: COPY --from=build /bin/cicado /home/cicado/cicado
nodes.summary: Copies the compiled cicado CLI binary from the build stage into the runner runtime image alongside cicado-runner.

nodes.name: EXPOSE 9090
nodes.summary: Documents the runner image's gRPC listener port used to dial the server.

nodes.name: ENTRYPOINT ["/home/cicado/cicado-runner"]
nodes.summary: Sets the runner image's entrypoint to the cicado-runner binary.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Development stack (`make dev`) wiring the CICaDo server, Postgres, and one runner together with healthchecks so a demo job travels the whole path with no manual bootstrap; explicitly not suitable for production (plaintext DB password, no TLS, constant registration token).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses healthcheck + depends_on condition: service_healthy to sequence Postgres -> server -> runner startup; fsync/full_page_writes/synchronous_commit are disabled on Postgres purely to speed up the dev/test loop, not for correctness.

nodes.name: postgres
nodes.summary: postgres:16-alpine service seeded with the cicado/cicado/cicado user/password/db, with durability settings disabled for speed and a pg_isready healthcheck gating dependents.

nodes.name: server
nodes.summary: Builds the Dockerfile's `server` target and runs cicado-server with dev-only flags (CICADO_MIGRATE, CICADO_DEV_SEED, CICADO_INSECURE_WEBHOOK) exposing HTTP :8080 and gRPC :8081, gated on Postgres being healthy.

nodes.name: runner
nodes.summary: Builds the Dockerfile's `runner` target and runs cicado-runner against the dev server with a well-known registration token and insecure (no-TLS) gRPC, gated on the server being healthy.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: Bootstrap GitHub Actions CI (runs until CICaDo can dogfood its own builds per CIC-29): five parallel jobs build/vet, lint, race-test against a real Postgres service, validate the frozen runner protocol (ADR-004), and build both Docker images, on every push to master and every pull request.
nodes.languageNotes: The concurrency group cancels an in-flight run only on non-master refs, so every commit landed on master still gets a complete result. The protocol-breaking check compares the checked-out ref against github.event.before on a master push (since origin/master already IS the new tip) but against origin/master on a pull_request, and treats an all-zero github.event.before (new branch / rewritten history) as nothing-to-compare rather than a failure.

nodes.name: Build and vet
nodes.summary: Compiles the whole module tree, runs `go vet`, then runs `make tidy` and fails if it produced any diff in go.mod/go.sum across both the root and tools/ modules.

nodes.name: Lint
nodes.summary: Installs pinned tooling via `make dev-deps` and runs `golangci-lint` across the whole module.

nodes.name: Test (race)
nodes.summary: Runs the full suite with `go test -race` against a real postgres:16-alpine service container, then parses the `go test -json` event stream to fail the build if any database-backed test silently skipped (distinguished from a package that legitimately has no test files), so CI cannot go green having tested almost nothing.

nodes.name: Protocol
nodes.summary: Lints the Protobuf schema with buf, verifies generated code is up to date via `make generate-check`, and enforces ADR-004's frozen runner protocol by rejecting breaking changes — comparing against the pre-push SHA on a master push or the PR base branch on a pull request.

nodes.name: Docker images
nodes.summary: Builds both the server and runner Docker image targets (without pushing) using GitHub Actions layer caching; grants itself `actions: write` to make that cache usable since the workflow-level permissions otherwise lock every scope to none.

nodes.name: 0001_init.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration establishing CICaDo's entire v1 schema: tenancy (orgs/repos/workflows), the runner fleet, the runs/jobs/steps execution model where the jobs table doubles as the job queue (ADR-002), the status/log streaming tables, secrets, tokens, and the audit log, plus the LISTEN/NOTIFY trigger that wakes dispatchers.
nodes.languageNotes: The jobs table has no separate queue store: claiming is FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED against a partial index (jobs_claim_idx), the lease_id column is the sole execution authority (regenerated per claim so a zombie runner's stale lease is distinguishable from a legitimate re-run), and a CHECK constraint (jobs_lease_consistency) ties claimed/running status to a non-null lease_id so no code path can set one half of that pair and forget the other.

nodes.name: orgs
nodes.summary: Tenancy root: org id, slug, and name. Every other entity (repos, runners, secrets, tokens, audit_events) is scoped to one of these via org_id.

nodes.name: repos
nodes.summary: One row per forge repository (unique on org_id/forge/owner/name); carries the forge discriminator (only 'github' implemented in MVP), the GitHub App installation_id used to mint per-job tokens, and a run_counter bumped under the run-creation row lock so run numbers stay gapless and monotonic per repo.

nodes.name: workflows
nodes.summary: One row per workflow file discovered in a repo (unique on repo_id/path); stores both the raw YAML `source` and the parsed `definition` jsonb plus a content_sha, so the UI can show the exact bytes a run was produced from and the parser's positional errors point at something that still exists.

nodes.name: runners
nodes.summary: Registered runner agents: labels/executors/features are copied from the registration token at enrollment, never from the runner's own RegisterRequest, so a stolen token cannot self-assign privileged labels beyond what it was minted with; tracks capacity, status (online/draining/offline), and last heartbeat.

nodes.name: runs
nodes.summary: One row per workflow trigger (unique on repo_id/number); a status state machine (pending/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled), a trigger_source mirroring audit_events.surface so a run traces back to the click/slash-command/webhook that caused it, and is_fork, the input to the fork-PR policy that strips secrets and deploy identity.

nodes.name: jobs
nodes.summary: THE job queue (ADR-002) — no separate queue store exists. Carries status/executor/priority/timeout/env/secret-name-refs alongside lease_id/claimed_by/lease_expires_at/attempts queue-and-lease state and exit_code/watermark result state; a CHECK constraint (jobs_lease_consistency) enforces that claimed/running status if and only if lease_id is set, and last_lease_id is retained after completion so trailing log chunks that arrive after the terminal status can still authorize against the lease they were produced under.

nodes.name: job_dependencies
nodes.summary: The workflow `needs` DAG, stored as its own join table (job_id, depends_on_job_id) rather than a column on jobs so finding newly-eligible jobs is an index lookup, not a scan; a CHECK constraint forbids a job depending on itself.

nodes.name: steps
nodes.summary: Individual executable steps within a job (unique on job_id/step_index): image (digest-pinned when the workflow provided one), command, per-step env and timeout, and a server-controlled network_enabled flag that defaults off regardless of what the job requested.

nodes.name: job_status_updates
nodes.summary: Append-only, idempotent status stream keyed by the protocol's own (job_id, seq) primary key, so a StatusUpdate redelivered after a runner reconnect hits the primary key and is a no-op rather than a duplicate state transition; runner_ts is advisory only, kept for diagnosing clock skew.

nodes.name: log_entries
nodes.summary: Log chunks and structured events share one sequence space per job (job_id, seq) so a single watermark covers both and replay after a reconnect is totally ordered; a CHECK constraint (log_entries_shape) enforces that a row is exactly one of a chunk (data+io set) or an event (event_kind+event_json set). Chunk `data` is redacted at ingest, before this insert — nothing unredacted is ever written here.

nodes.name: log_archives
nodes.summary: Records where a job's logs went after the hot log_entries rows were compacted and pruned to blob storage; reads fall through to the archived object transparently once the hot rows are gone.

nodes.name: secrets
nodes.summary: Envelope-encrypted secret values: ciphertext plus a KMS-wrapped data key stored beside it so key rotation is a per-row rewrap. A CHECK constraint (secrets_scope_shape) enforces the org/repo/environment scope shape. Write-only from the API's point of view — no endpoint returns `ciphertext`; the only read path is job dispatch behind a live lease.

nodes.name: tokens
nodes.summary: Every bearer secret in the system — registration, runner, job, MCP, and API tokens — hashed (SHA-256) in one table, giving one revocation path, one expiry check, and one audit point; the presented value is shown to the operator once at mint time and is not recoverable from token_hash.

nodes.name: audit_events
nodes.summary: Every state-changing action from every surface (web/chat/mcp/api/forge/system) lands here, recording only payload_hash rather than the raw payload since payloads can contain secret material, so the audit trail stays safe to read widely.

nodes.name: runners_org_status_idx
nodes.summary: Lookup index on (org_id, status) for listing an org's runners by state.

nodes.name: runners_heartbeat_idx
nodes.summary: Partial index on last_heartbeat_at for online/draining runners, used to detect stalled runners.

nodes.name: runs_repo_created_idx
nodes.summary: Index on (repo_id, created_at DESC) backing a repo's run-history feed.

nodes.name: runs_status_idx
nodes.summary: Partial index on status, scoped to pending/running runs only.

nodes.name: jobs_claim_idx
nodes.summary: Partial index on (priority, created_at) for status='queued', ordered to exactly match the claim query's ORDER BY so FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED can stop at LIMIT; stays proportional to queue depth rather than to all job history.

nodes.name: jobs_lease_expiry_idx
nodes.summary: Partial index on lease_expires_at for claimed/running jobs; the sweeper uses it to find leases that expired without reaching a terminal status.

nodes.name: jobs_run_idx
nodes.summary: Index on run_id for looking up a run's jobs.

nodes.name: jobs_claimed_by_idx
nodes.summary: Partial index on claimed_by (non-null) for a runner's currently-claimed jobs.

nodes.name: job_dependencies_depends_on_idx
nodes.summary: Reverse-lookup index on depends_on_job_id for finding a job's dependents.

nodes.name: log_entries_step_idx
nodes.summary: Index on (job_id, step_index, seq) for reading one step's log stream in order.

nodes.name: secrets_scope_name_idx
nodes.summary: Unique index folding nullable repo_id/environment to fixed sentinels so two NULLs compare equal, preventing two org-scoped secrets from silently sharing a name.

nodes.name: tokens_kind_org_idx
nodes.summary: Index on (kind, org_id) for listing an org's tokens by kind.

nodes.name: CIC-103-dag-run-rollup.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-103: a single `advanceRun` helper in `server/queue`, called from every terminal job transition (Complete, Requeue, TerminalizeCancel), promotes `needs`-dependent jobs from pending to queued and rolls a run up to a terminal `runs.status` once all its jobs finish.

nodes.name: CIC-106-backpressure-run-terminal.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-106 fixing a backpressure bug: a per-repo run slot is now held from webhook receipt until the run reaches a terminal state (via the CIC-103 run-terminal hook) instead of being released milliseconds later when the webhook handler returns.

nodes.name: CIC-107-step-if-conditions.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-107: since the cicanscript runner is not yet wired to honor step-level `if: failure|always` conditions, the workflow validator rejects them on every step until the runner implementation and protocol field land.

nodes.name: CIC-120-producer-wiring.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-120: wires the existing `GitHubWorkflowProducer` into `cicado-server`'s `main.go` so `Config.Producer` is actually constructed, closing the gap where a nil producer silently fell back to the dev-seed demo workflow instead of fetching real repo workflows.

nodes.name: CIC-121-cicado-workflow-path.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-121: CICaDo workflow files move from `.github/workflows/` to `.cicado/workflows/` (top-level only, `.yml`/`.yaml`) so CICaDo workflows no longer trigger spurious GitHub Actions runs or get fed GitHub Actions' own YAML files.

nodes.name: CIC-135-embedded-secret-refs.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-135: embedded `${{ secrets.NAME }}` references inside a larger string value (e.g. a bearer header) are now interpolated in place for GitHub Actions parity, via a new `internal/secretexpr` package whose `Resolve`/`Refs`/`NamesIn` helpers also feed `GetJobSecrets` authorization.

nodes.name: CIC-38-getjobsecrets-rpc.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-38: implements `secrets.Postgres` (AES-256-GCM, nonce-ciphertext-tag blob) against the `secrets` table and wires it into `runnersvc.Service.GetJobSecrets`, which previously always returned an empty response despite a correct lease check.

nodes.name: CIC-39-oidc-issuer.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-39: a standalone OIDC token issuer package that mints short-lived, self-contained job credentials for `identity: aws`-style jobs to exchange via `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`; explicitly a leaf package only, with no server wiring, runner change, or HTTP endpoint yet.

nodes.name: CIC-40-per-job-ephemeral-tokens.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-40: new `server/jobtoken` package issues short-lived, hashed-at-rest bearer tokens scoped to (org, run, job, branch) plus read/write scopes, via a `Store`-backed `Manager` with a fail-closed `Auditor` on every issue, revoke, and verified use.

nodes.name: CIC-41-audit.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-41: new `server/audit` package providing an append-only, SHA-256 hash-chained audit log (`MemoryLog` for MVP) that records every state-changing action with principal, source surface, and payload hash, with `Chain.Verify()` detecting tampering.

nodes.name: CIC-69-decisions-policy.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-69: establishes the per-PR decision-log policy itself — new decisions are written as individual `docs/decisions/CIC-NN-*.md` files rather than inserted at a single shared marker in `CLAUDE.md`, eliminating the N-1 merge conflicts per cycle that the old pattern produced.

nodes.name: CIC-71a-controller-dispatcher.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-71a (CIC-71 sub-blocker 1): introduces `server/controller` as the first real `webhook.Dispatcher`, replacing `webhook.NoOpDispatcher`, creating a `runs` row on push/PR events and reporting it to the configured `forge.Forge`, gated by `backpressure.Tracker`.

nodes.name: CIC-71b-real-org-lookup.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-71b (CIC-71 sub-blocker 2): adds real `store.ResolveRepo`, `store.UpsertOrg`, and `store.FindOrgBySlug` so `controller.resolveRepo` looks up genuine org/repo rows instead of the CIC-71a prototype's deterministic SHA-1 pseudo-UUID.

nodes.name: CIC-71c-workflow-dag.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-71c (CIC-71 sub-blocker 3): adds a `WorkflowLoader` interface (`StaticLoader` plus a skeleton `StoreLoader`) and wires `LoadAndCreateJobs` into `HandlePush`/`HandlePullRequest`, so each created run matches its repo's workflows against the triggering event and builds the job DAG.

nodes.name: CIC-71d-server-wiring.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-71d (CIC-71 sub-blocker 4): replaces `webhook.NoOpDispatcher{}` in `cmd/cicado-server/main.go` with `controller.New(st, NoOpForge{}, controller.DefaultConfig(), log)`, wiring the real controller into the server while deferring a genuine Forge implementation.

nodes.name: CIC-71e-store-loader.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-71e (CIC-71 sub-blocker 5): adds `store.WorkflowRow` and `store.ListWorkflowsForRepo`, completing `StoreLoader.LoadAll` in `server/controller/jobs.go` to decode the `Definition` jsonb column into `*workflow.Workflow` instead of re-parsing YAML.

nodes.name: CIC-71f-audit-wiring.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-71f (CIC-71 sub-blocker 6): adds an `audit.Log` to the controller's `Config` and emits a new `ActionCreateRun` audit entry, non-fatally, whenever `HandlePush` or `HandlePullRequest` successfully creates a run.

nodes.name: CIC-71g-backpressure-wiring.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-71g (CIC-71 sub-blocker 7): adds a `*backpressure.Tracker` to `dispatch.Config` and calls `Tracker.Acquire` in `dispatchOnce` for every claimed job, requeuing with `UndeliveredBackoff` when the per-repo cap is exceeded; a nil tracker is a no-op.

nodes.name: CIC-71h-approvalgates-wiring.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-71h (CIC-71 sub-blocker 8, final): adds a `*approvalgates.Manager` to `controller.Config` and calls `maybeOpenGate` at the end of `HandlePullRequest` for every PR run, as a placeholder ahead of a future policy layer deciding which runs require approval.

nodes.name: CIC-72-artifacts-migration.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for CIC-72: adds migration `0003_artifacts.sql` defining the `artifacts` table (org/run/job foreign keys, blob_key, size, content type, expiry) that `server/artifacts/postgres.go` already queried against but which had never been created.

nodes.name: CIC-73-presigned-url-defer.md
nodes.summary: Decision record deferring the production S3 presigned-URL driver to M9, documenting why MemoryPreSigner is the only implementation of PreSignedURLProvider until then.

nodes.name: CIC-74-masker-wiring.md
nodes.summary: Decision record fixing two log-redaction defects: runnersvc.DefaultConfig defaulting to NoopMasker, and InstallationTokenMinter never registering minted tokens with the masker.

nodes.name: CIC-75-audit-postgres.md
nodes.summary: Decision record for the Postgres-backed audit log implementation (PostgresLog), documenting two review-blocking bugs fixed: a missing SQL type cast and an ID-inclusion hash-chain break.

nodes.name: CIC-76-mcp-defer.md
nodes.summary: Decision record deferring the full MCP JSON-RPC transport to M9, noting that the underlying Go-method tool handlers in server/mcp are complete but unreachable by external MCP clients.

nodes.name: CIC-77-knowledge-graph-currency.md
nodes.summary: Process-convention decision establishing the per-PR cadence for keeping the /understand knowledge graph in .ua/ in lockstep with master via /understand-diff and /understand.

nodes.name: CIC-78-workflow-loader-wiring.md
nodes.summary: Decision record wiring the store-backed workflow loader into main.go and fixing two silent job-creation gaps: an unwritten workflows table and a NULL secret_refs/required_tags constraint violation.

nodes.name: CIC-79-secrets-delivery.md
nodes.summary: Decision record closing the gap that let no workflow reference secrets.FOO: adds server-side secret_refs extraction and runner-side GetJobSecrets fetch plus secrets.X resolution, with follow-up security fixes for fork-PR leakage.

nodes.name: CIC-80-webhook-fail-closed.md
nodes.summary: Security decision record making webhook HMAC verification fail closed (401) when CICADO_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty, unless the operator explicitly opts into --insecure-webhook.

nodes.name: CIC-81-forge-wiring.md
nodes.summary: Decision record wiring the GitHub Checks forge into the run lifecycle: Prepare before job creation, Complete on run-terminal, and replay-based handling of check_suite/check_run re-run requests.

nodes.name: CIC-82-wire-built-subsystems.md
nodes.summary: Decision record wiring the previously-unwired per-job SSE log route and runnersvc.LogPublish so live, masked log lines reach connected viewers; defers dispatcher backpressure to a separate ticket.

nodes.name: CIC-83-stale-todos-lambda-stub.md
nodes.summary: QC disposition record resolving or re-attributing five stale/misattributed TODO comments across the codebase and making the unimplemented Lambda dispatch stub fail closed instead of silently reporting success.

nodes.name: CIC-84-workflow-producer.md
nodes.summary: Design decision for the production workflow producer: a GitHub contents fetcher plus controller/store wiring that fills the workflows table from .cicado/workflows/*.yml at the triggering SHA before job loading.

nodes.name: CIC-85-zero-match-finalisation.md
nodes.summary: Decision record fixing runs that match zero workflows by adding store.FinalizeRunToSucceeded, called from LoadAndCreateJobs so such runs terminate instead of staying pending forever.

nodes.name: ADR-000-template.md
nodes.summary: Template and authoring process for Architecture Decision Records: required sections (Context, Decision, Rationale, Consequences), naming convention, immutability rule (supersede, never delete), and the instruction to add new ADRs to the README index in the same PR.

nodes.name: ADR-001-language-go.md
nodes.summary: Accepted decision to use Go for both the server and runner, citing single-binary distribution, concurrency fit for scheduler/log-streaming workloads, and mature AWS/Docker SDKs; confines TypeScript to nothing and reserves Rust only for a possible future sandboxing component.

nodes.name: ADR-002-postgres-queue.md
nodes.summary: Accepted decision making Postgres the sole database and job queue (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claiming, LISTEN/NOTIFY, visibility-timeout sweep), behind a Go Queue interface, to avoid a dual-write problem and an extra stateful dependency.

nodes.name: ADR-003-frontend-no-build.md
nodes.summary: Accepted decision for a no-build frontend: Go html/template server rendering via embed.FS, vendored htmx, SSE (not WebSockets) for live data, and hand-written vanilla ES-module islands for the log viewer and DAG view; supersedes an earlier React/TypeScript recommendation.

nodes.name: ADR-004-runner-protocol.md
nodes.summary: Accepted decision for an outbound-only gRPC streaming runner protocol over TLS with protobuf versioning and N-1 server compatibility; carries a 2026-09-16 amendment splitting control (Session) and bulk logs (LogStream) into separate streams to prevent head-of-line blocking.

nodes.name: ADR-005-plugin-model.md
nodes.summary: Accepted decision that plugins are OCI images with capability manifests (deny-by-default network/secrets/mounts), referenced by digest with cosign signing for a verified tier, and that no third-party code ever runs in-process in the control plane; notes a post-MVP Wasm tier.

nodes.name: ADR-006-license.md
nodes.summary: Accepted decision that the core platform is Apache-2.0 permanently, citing Drone's relicensing fallout and Earthly's shutdown as cautionary precedent; any future monetization must come via clearly separate enterprise add-ons, never relicensing the core.

nodes.name: ADR-007-name-cicado.md
nodes.summary: Accepted decision naming the product CICaDo (binary `cicado`), documenting the trademark/collision research that eliminated earlier candidates (CICaDa, Cinch, Katydid, Magicicada, CadenCI), the clearance findings, and a registration checklist for domains/org/social handles.

nodes.name: ADR-008-migrations-goose-embedded.md
nodes.summary: Accepted decision to use goose as a Go library with migrations embedded in the server binary via embed.FS (applied through `cicado-server migrate up`), chosen over Atlas/tern/golang-migrate to preserve the one-binary install promise and goose's advisory-lock safety under concurrent rolling-deploy starts.

nodes.name: RegisterRequest
nodes.summary: Request to enroll a new runner, carrying the registration token, a display name, and declared capabilities.

nodes.name: Capabilities
nodes.summary: Declares a runner's supported executors, OS/arch, version, and feature flags used for protocol capability negotiation.

nodes.name: RegisterResponse
nodes.summary: Response to a successful registration carrying the assigned runner ID, its long-lived credential, and label set.

nodes.name: RunnerMessage
nodes.summary: Envelope for every message a runner sends up the bidirectional session stream (hello, job ack, status update, heartbeat).

nodes.name: ServerMessage
nodes.summary: Envelope for every message the server sends down the bidirectional session stream (hello, job assignment, status ack, cancel, throttle, update notice).

nodes.name: Hello
nodes.summary: Initial runner handshake message carrying the protocol version, capabilities, and optional resume state.

nodes.name: ResumeState
nodes.summary: Carries the job/lease and last-acked log/status sequence numbers a runner uses to resume a session after reconnect.

nodes.name: ServerHello
nodes.summary: Server's handshake reply: session ID, heartbeat interval, limits, resume verdicts, and supported runner version range.

nodes.name: Limits
nodes.summary: Server-imposed limits on log chunk size, inflight chunk count, and journal disk usage.

nodes.name: ResumeVerdict
nodes.summary: Per-job verdict on whether a runner's resume attempt is accepted, along with log/status watermarks to replay from.

nodes.name: JobAssignment
nodes.summary: Assigns a job and lease to a runner along with its full job spec.

nodes.name: JobSpec
nodes.summary: Full specification for a job: run ID, workflow name, steps, secret references, timeout, executor, and git context.

nodes.name: StepSpec
nodes.summary: Specification for a single job step: image, command, per-step timeout, and network access flag.

nodes.name: GitContext
nodes.summary: Clone URL, ref, and commit SHA a runner needs to check out the job's source.

nodes.name: JobAck
nodes.summary: Runner's acknowledgment (or rejection) of a job assignment.

nodes.name: StatusUpdate
nodes.summary: Sequenced status update for a job/step: state, exit code, and error classification detail.

nodes.name: StatusAck
nodes.summary: Server's ack of the highest status-update sequence number it has durably received.

nodes.name: Heartbeat
nodes.summary: Periodic runner liveness signal carrying active job IDs and host resource stats.

nodes.name: HostStats
nodes.summary: CPU load, memory, and disk-free snapshot reported in a runner heartbeat.

nodes.name: CancelJob
nodes.summary: Server-initiated cancellation of a job with a reason and grace period.

nodes.name: Throttle
nodes.summary: Server directive capping a runner's log upload rate for a given job.

nodes.name: UpdateNotice
nodes.summary: Advertises the minimum supported and latest runner versions, with an operator-facing message.

nodes.name: LogUp
nodes.summary: Envelope for a runner's log-stream upload: either a raw log chunk or a structured event.

nodes.name: LogChunk
nodes.summary: A sequenced chunk of raw stdout/stderr bytes for a specific job step.

nodes.name: StructuredEvent
nodes.summary: A sequenced structured event (JSON payload) emitted for a job step, e.g. step_started/step_finished/error_classified.

nodes.name: LogAck
nodes.summary: Server's ack of the highest log-sequence number it has durably received for a job.

nodes.name: GetJobSecretsRequest
nodes.summary: Request for the secret values a leased job is authorized to receive, scoped to the live lease.

nodes.name: RunnerService.Register
nodes.summary: Unary RPC where a runner exchanges its registration token for a runner ID and long-lived credential.

nodes.name: RunnerService.Session
nodes.summary: Bidirectional streaming RPC carrying the runner/server control-plane session: hello, job assignment, status, heartbeat, cancellation.

nodes.name: RunnerService.LogStream

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: CICaDo is an open-source, self-hostable CI/CD platform built around three differentiators: operational simplicity (two Go binaries, Postgres as the only stateful dependency), ChatOps-native Slack integration, and AI-agent-native MCP tooling. The README lays out the repository layout and points to project-docs/ as the architectural source of truth — the roadmap this tour follows.

tour.title: Three Binaries, One Codebase
tour.description: CICaDo compiles to three Go binaries from one module: the server (control plane), the runner agent, and the `cicado` CLI. The server's main.go wires together the store, queue, forge, webhook receiver, and HTTP/gRPC listeners; the runner's main.go loads its enrolled identity and dials the server; the CLI's main.go exposes workflow validation standalone. Starting here establishes the processes you'll trace through the rest of the tour.
tour.languageLesson: Go programs with multiple independently-built binaries use separate `cmd/<binary>/main.go` packages sharing one module, so each binary pulls in only the packages it imports rather than one monolithic executable.

tour.title: Workflow Definition & Validation
tour.description: Before a job can run, its workflow YAML must parse into a valid DAG. workflow-v1.json is the JSON Schema that defines what a legal workflow looks like; validate.go enforces structural rules (non-empty triggers, uses/run exclusivity, valid if-conditions) beyond what the schema alone can express; dag.go resolves each job's `needs` graph with Kahn's algorithm, detecting cycles and computing fan-out/fan-in levels. This is the first gate every pushed commit passes through.
tour.languageLesson: Go's error handling favors aggregating multiple violations into one typed error (here, ValidationError) rather than failing fast on the first problem — giving the user every YAML mistake in one response, echoing the project's stated UX differentiator over GitHub Actions' silent failures.

tour.title: Postgres as the Job Queue
tour.description: ADR-002 locks in a deliberately unusual decision: Postgres is not just storage, it IS the job queue — no Redis, SQS, or Kafka. queue.go defines the storage-agnostic Queue interface; postgres.go implements claiming via `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, lease renewal, and requeue-with-backoff; listen.go wraps Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY so waiting dispatchers wake immediately instead of polling. Together these three files are the mechanism behind the server's single-stateful-dependency promise from Step 1.
tour.languageLesson: SQL's `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` lets multiple concurrent consumers each claim a different row without blocking on each other — the classic pattern for building a job queue directly on a relational database.

tour.title: The Database Schema
tour.description: 0001_init.sql is the migration that establishes the entire v1 schema in one file: tenancy (orgs/repos/workflows), the runner fleet, and critically the jobs table that doubles as the queue from Step 4, complete with the LISTEN/NOTIFY trigger that wakes dispatchers. store.go opens the connection pool against this schema, and runs.go is the write path: it creates a run with its whole job DAG inside one transaction, flipping top-level jobs to 'queued' to fire that same trigger.
tour.languageLesson: Goose-style numbered SQL migrations (0001_init.sql, 0002_..., 0003_...) apply incrementally and in order, so the schema's history is reconstructable by replaying files — each migration should be idempotent where possible and never edited after it ships.

tour.title: Run Controller & Dispatch
tour.description: controller.go is where external events become work: it implements webhook.Dispatcher, turning a decoded GitHub push or pull_request into a run and its job DAG via jobs.go's LoadAndCreateJobs, which parses, validates (Step 3), and persists (Step 5) in one pipeline. Once jobs are queued, dispatcher.go's background loop claims them from the Postgres queue (Step 4) and assigns them to a connected runner session — the bridge from control plane to runner agent.

tour.title: The Frozen Runner Protocol & Agent
tour.description: runner.proto is ADR-004's frozen contract: the gRPC definitions for runner registration, the bidirectional session stream, log/event streaming, and job-secret retrieval — additive changes only, ever. service.go is the control-plane side that implements this protocol, authorizing secret delivery only against a live lease (the security invariant from CLAUDE.md). job.go is the runner-side counterpart: it accepts a JobAssignment, resolves secrets, executes each step, and streams status back over the session this protocol defines.
tour.languageLesson: Protobuf field numbers are permanent — once shipped, a field's number is never reused even if the field is later removed (marked `reserved` instead), which is exactly how ADR-004's freeze is enforced at the wire-format level across server and runner releases that may not upgrade in lockstep.

tour.title: Forge & Webhook Integration
tour.description: receiver.go is the HTTP handler GitHub's webhooks hit: it verifies the HMAC-SHA256 signature fail-closed and hands decoded events to the Controller from Step 6. forge.go defines the Forge interface — Prepare/Start/Complete/Rerun/CloneCredentialsForRun — so CICaDo isn't hard-wired to one git host; checks.go is GitHub's concrete implementation, reporting check-run status back to the PR that triggered the run.

tour.title: Secrets & Audit
tour.description: Two of CLAUDE.md's security invariants live here in code. secrets.go defines a Store where decrypted values are reachable only through a time-limited Lease authorized against the live job lease from Step 7 — never a plaintext API; postgres.go is the persisted, AES-256-GCM-encrypted backing implementation. audit.go is the hash-chained audit log: every entry commits to the hash of the one before it, so tampering with history is detectable, satisfying the 'every state-changing action writes an audit event' rule.
tour.languageLesson: A hash chain — each record's hash incorporating the previous record's hash — is the same structural idea behind blockchains and git commits: it turns 'was this log tampered with' into a single recomputation check over the whole chain.

tour.title: Containerization & CI Pipeline
tour.description: The Dockerfile is a multi-stage build that compiles all three binaries (Step 2) once, then splits into a minimal distroless server image and a debian-slim runner image carrying git and a shell for executing job steps. ci.yml and the root Makefile are CICaDo testing itself: five parallel CI jobs build/vet, lint, race-test against a real Postgres (Step 5), validate the frozen protocol (Step 7), and build these same Docker images on every push — the capstone that ties the whole tour's architecture back together under test.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Dockerfiles use multiple FROM statements: an early stage has the full toolchain to compile, while the final stage copies only the compiled binary into a minimal base image, keeping the shipped image small and reducing its attack surface.
